clue.text: Spider in car had hidden

indicators.note: the letters of the words in front are concealed under a disguise, rearranged out of sight

parts.note: taken as written, part of the fodder
taken as written, part of the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone found a spider lurking inside their car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden' looks like a hidden-word signal, but no run of letters gives the answer: it disguises IN plus CAR HAD as a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider belongs to the class of eight-legged arthropods, so it is one example of the group.

clue.text: Discomfited from morning in an outbuilding

indicators.note: the morning abbreviation is placed within the phrase for an outbuilding

parts.note: A plus SHED, a garden outbuilding
AM, ante meridiem, is the morning

explanation.surface: Someone retreats embarrassed after a morning spent in the garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be discomfited is to feel embarrassed and shamed, so the adjective matches.

clue.text: A royal scout's organizers

parts.note: R is the usual abbreviation for royal, as in RN or RAF
a Ranger is a senior member of the Scout or Guide movement; the possessive gives the S

explanation.surface: A royal scout's helpers are running the event.
explanation.definitionFit: Organizers set things in order, as people who arrange events or music do.

clue.text: Henley's first boat-crews are the tops

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the regatta's name is wanted here

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen; Henley is the famous Thames rowing regatta

explanation.surface: At Henley Royal Regatta, the leading rowing crews are the best of all.
explanation.walkthrough: Henley is the English town on the Thames whose summer rowing regatta races eights.
explanation.definitionFit: Heights are the highest points, the summits or tops of something.

clue.text: Enamelled cutter in set, displayed in fun?

definitions.text: Enamelled cutter in set, displayed in fun?

parts.words: Enamelled cutter in set, displayed in fun?
parts.note: a front tooth, coated in enamel and used for biting, sits in a set of teeth and shows when someone grins with amusement

explanation.surface: A glazed blade from a set is put on show as a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A front tooth for biting is a cutter covered in enamel, part of the dental set seen in a smile.

clue.text: Transferring by lease of half to a quarter

parts.note: demi- is a prefix meaning half
SE, south-east, is a quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone sublets half their property to cover a quarter of the costs.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, to demise property is to convey it by lease, so the noun names that transfer.

clue.text: Opera that does not open — in the red — refusing admission

indicators.note: the shortened opera is placed within the word for the red

parts.note: being in the red means being in debt

indicators.note: the opera loses its opening letter

parts.note: Carmen is Bizet's opera

explanation.surface: An opera house fails to open its doors because it is in financial trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Bizet's opera Carmen; the dashes make 'in the red' look like an aside, but being in the red means being in debt, which is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Debarment is the act of barring or excluding someone, a refusal of entry.

clue.text: Many supplementing such a novel crowd

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a crossword shorthand for many
adding to something supplements it

explanation.surface: A large number of people join a crowd in a new way.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hardy's novel is Far from the Madding Crowd, so the crowd in that title is described by this word.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardy's title uses this adjective, meaning frenzied, for the crowd in his book.

clue.text: Second request for a sprinkler

parts.note: a prayer is an earnest request

explanation.surface: Someone asks a second time for a garden sprinkler.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that sprays water, as on a lawn, is a sprinkler.

clue.text: Solitary hard-top in the Strand, say?

definitions.text: Solitary hard-top in the Strand, say?

parts.words: Solitary hard-top in the Strand, say?
parts.note: a creature living alone in a borrowed hard shell on the shore, strand meaning beach rather than the London street

explanation.surface: A lone car with a hardtop roof is parked in the Strand, the London street.
explanation.walkthrough: The Strand looks like the London street; here strand is a beach, where this shell-borrowing crustacean lives.
explanation.definitionFit: This crustacean lives alone inside a borrowed shell, a hard covering, on the seashore.

clue.text: River race

explanation.surface: A short note about a river race.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dart is a river in Devon; to dart is to rush or race quickly.

clue.text: Synthetic cream all over their blue shirts!

definitions.text: Synthetic cream all over their blue shirts!

indicators.note: the letters are scattered all over the place, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, part of the fodder
taken as written, part of the fodder

explanation.surface: A football team's sky-blue shirts are smeared with fake cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over' rearranges SYNTHETIC CREAM; the whole clue points to a football club famous for playing in sky blue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Manchester football club is known as the Sky Blues for its blue home strip.

clue.text: Surgeon's assistant with back to the wall

explanation.surface: A surgeon's helper stands with their back against the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A dresser assists a surgeon by dressing wounds; a kitchen sideboard of shelves stands against a wall.

clue.text: Excuse from unit duty

parts.note: ex means from, as in ex works
one is a single unit
a rate is a tax or duty levied

explanation.surface: Someone is let off duty in a military unit.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate is to free from blame or obligation, to let off.

clue.text: Moth harboured in near poverty

indicators.note: the moth is held within the word for near

parts.note: by means near, as in close by
the eggar is a kind of large moth

explanation.surface: A moth lives in a house close to destitution.
explanation.definitionFit: Beggary is the state of extreme want, being reduced to begging.

clue.text: A Maine car smashed all Uncle Sam's things

indicators.note: the letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written, part of the fodder
taken as written, part of the fodder

explanation.surface: A car from Maine crashes, wrecking everything an American owned.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncle Sam personifies the United States; 'smashed' rearranges MAINE CAR into MERICANA after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: Americana are artefacts and objects characteristic of the United States.

clue.text: Mainstay in boats at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, part of the fodder
taken as written, part of the fodder

explanation.surface: The main support for the crew is aboard boats out at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A bastion is a stronghold, so figuratively a chief support or mainstay.

clue.text: Tumbler sometimes seen on the bars

definitions.text: Tumbler sometimes seen on the bars

parts.words: Tumbler sometimes seen on the bars
parts.note: a tumbler here is a gymnast performing on parallel bars, not a drinking glass in a pub

explanation.surface: A drinking glass is often left standing on pub counters.
explanation.walkthrough: Tumbler and bars suggest a glass in a pub; the tumbler is a gymnast on the bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymnast who tumbles and performs on bars or trapezes is an acrobat.

clue.text: Field adviser

parts.note: someone who advises punters on which runner in a race field to back

explanation.surface: An agricultural consultant advises farmers.
explanation.walkthrough: Field suggests farming; in racing the field is the set of runners in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing pundits recommend horses from the field to bettors.

clue.text: What may be picked up by the beak?

definitions.text: What may be picked up by the beak?

parts.words: What may be picked up by the beak?
parts.note: beak is British slang for a magistrate, who may draw a regular salary rather than being an unpaid volunteer

explanation.surface: A bird pecks up food with its bill.
explanation.walkthrough: Beak suggests a bird; in British slang it is a magistrate, and a stipendiary magistrate is a salaried one.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed salary, especially for a clergyman or magistrate, is collected as regular pay.

clue.text: Shift nurse is Dawn

indicators.note: the letters are shifted around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, part of the fodder
taken as written, part of the fodder

explanation.surface: A nurse called Dawn is changing shifts.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn is daybreak, the time the sun comes up.

clue.text: Characters leaning forwards to point to foreign words

definitions.text: Characters leaning forwards to point to foreign words

parts.words: Characters leaning forwards to point to foreign words
parts.note: printed letters that slope to the right, used to mark words borrowed from other languages

explanation.surface: People bending forward to indicate words in a foreign language.
explanation.walkthrough: Characters suggests people; they are printed letters, slanted type used for foreign terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloping type is used in print to mark foreign words and emphasis.

clue.text: Most penetrating flower blight

parts.note: a river is something that flows, a flower; the Dee is a river
a pest is a blight or plague

explanation.surface: A plant disease attacks a flower most deeply.
explanation.walkthrough: Flower is a crossword pun for a river, the thing that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of deep describes what goes furthest in, most profound.

clue.text: Typical agent

explanation.surface: A note about a run-of-the-mill agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Representative means typical of a class; a representative also acts as an agent for others.

clue.text: Back in Lincoln Square

parts.note: Abe was the nickname of Abraham Lincoln
a T-square, so T stands for square

explanation.surface: Someone retreats into Lincoln Square.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to support or encourage someone, to back them.

clue.text: Look forward to caper with one penny tea-roll

parts.note: an antic is a caper or prank
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the word tea is rolled over into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone looks forward to a lark with a penny teacake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roll' looks like a bread roll; it rearranges TEA into ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To anticipate is to expect something, to await it eagerly.

clue.text: Feel the cold fast

explanation.surface: Someone shivers while going without food.
explanation.definitionFit: In dialect, to starve is to be numb with cold; to starve is also to go without food, to fast.

clue.text: Channelled intelligence

parts.note: information sent out over a broadcasting channel, intelligence meaning news

explanation.surface: Information routed through official channels.
explanation.walkthrough: Intelligence means news here, and channelled refers to a television channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast of the news on radio or television delivers information.
